say:0:1910629201:1.text: Between the time gaps of the wishes, the Deepfolk once worshipped a deity, most likely the Mother Goddess. However, that faith was erased, or simply withered away with time.

say:1:1910629202:1.text: You infer that the Mother Goddess was not always worshipped by the Merfolk. She belonged to one particular age. The faithlessness of the Merfolk today means the memory and the worship of her have been ground away by the long years.

say:2:1910629203:1.text: The inscriptions have gaps in time, and the earliest of them predates the arrival of the Deepfolk. In other words, the Graveborn was already here before they came. The age when he carved his wish is older than the entire records of the Deepfolk.

say:3:1910629204:1.text: The gaps in the wishes mean that after that Graveborn's time, there was a long stretch of time when no one inscribed anything at all, until the Deepfolk came here and began to record anew. By then, his time period was already far behind them.
